title: Variae Lectiones
author: Isidorus Hispaliensis
source: Translated by Claude from tmp1402.tmp1402.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: CAP. XIII. N. 1, inanimalium. Al., animalium rerum ; a!., inanimalium rerum. Ibid., fingitur. Cicero. Al., f. sicut Cicero. N. 2, et in tragoediis. At., et tragrediis; al., et tragædis.
passages.english: Chapter 13. No. 1, "of inanimate things" (inanimalium). Other [manuscripts read] "of animate things" (animalium rerum); others, "of inanimate things" (inanimalium rerum). Same place, "is fashioned. Cicero." Others, "is fashioned, as Cicero [says]." No. 2, "and in tragedies." Others, "and tragedies"; others, "and by tragedians."
passages.notes: Apparatus of variant readings; "Al." (alii) taken as "other [manuscripts]". "At.", "A!.", "a!." are scanning errors for "Al."; "tragrediis" read as "tragoediis".

passages.original: A!., numeralem. Ibid., in magnitudinem rationalem. A!.. om., a!., in m. rationabilem. N. 2, sunt quæ. At., sicut geometrae (al., geometrici) vocant, quæ. Ibid., continentur. At., add. : Quæ sunt juxta Platonem numero quinque. Trigonus, tetra- gonus, pentagonus, hexagonus, heptagonus. Jam octonarius in cubum, id est, in solidam pergil figuram. Numerabilis. N. 4, figurae... quinque. Al. om.
passages.english: Others, "numerical" (numeralem). Same place, "into a rational magnitude." Others omit; others, "into a rationable magnitude." No. 2, "are those which." Others, "as the geometers (others, 'geometricians') call [them], which." Same place, "are contained." Others add: "These, according to Plato, are five in number: triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon. Then the number eight passes into the cube, that is, into a solid figure." "Numerable." No. 4, "figures... five." Others omit.
passages.notes: "tetra- gonus" and "pergil" (pergit) are scanning errors. "Numerabilis" appears to be a separate lemma left without a number.

passages.original: N. 16, asseruit. A!.. asserunt. N. 17, gymnasium enim. AI., gymno enim. Num. 18, in scriptis. AI., in Scripturis. Ibid., ut Dionysius Stoicus. Al. om. N. 19, commeantem. AI., commanentem. Ibid., ut Maro. Al., ut Varro. N. 20, Judicem asserunt. A!., i. dixerunt. Ibid., ex atomis. Al. om. ex. N. ii, gubernet. Al., gubernat. Ibid., qui cum est. A!., quicunque est. Ibid., cum exit, emorimur. Al., cum exiit, et moritur.
passages.english: No. 16, asseruit [he asserted]. Other [manuscripts]: asserunt [they assert]. No. 17, gymnasium enim [for a gymnasium]. Others: gymno enim [for naked]. No. 18, in scriptis [in writings]. Others: in Scripturis [in the Scriptures]. Same [number], ut Dionysius Stoicus [as Dionysius the Stoic]. Others omit [it]. No. 19, commeantem [passing through]. Others: commanentem [abiding together]. Same, ut Maro [as Maro]. Others: ut Varro [as Varro]. No. 20, Judicem asserunt [they assert a judge]. Others: i[udicem] dixerunt [they called (him) judge]. Same, ex atomis [from atoms]. Others omit ex. No. 21, gubernet [may govern]. Others: gubernat [governs]. Same, qui cum est [which, when it is present]. Others: quicunque est [whoever it is]. Same, cum exit, emorimur [when it departs, we die]. Others: cum exiit, et moritur [when it has departed, he also dies].
passages.notes: This is a list of variant readings; the Latin lemmata and variants are kept, with English glosses in brackets. 'A!.' and 'AI.' are scanning errors for 'Al.' (alii, 'other [manuscripts]'). 'N. ii' is read as 'N. 21', following the sequence of numbers. 'i.' in no. 20 is taken as an abbreviation of 'iudicem'.

passages.original: Ibid., a bono deterior. At., a bono melior. N. 178, quia mollior. A!., quasi mollior. Ibid., est monitor. A!., et monitor. Ibid., bona. Al., pœnam. Num. 179, mulcalor. At., mulctator. N. 180, Lucanus. Al., ut Lucanus. Ibid., veniat. At., veniam. Ibiid., enervato corpore dedecoret. Al., enervati corporis dedecore. N. 181, a mœchia. Al., a macia. Ibid., sive a maceratione. Al. om. Ibid., manu ancus. AI., manu ancus, vel manu cassus.
passages.english: Ibid., "a bono deterior" ["worse than good"]. Another [manuscript reads] "a bono melior" ["better than good"]. No. 178, "quia mollior" ["because softer"]. Another, "quasi mollior" ["as if softer"]. Ibid., "est monitor" ["is an adviser"]. Another, "et monitor" ["and an adviser"]. Ibid., "bona" ["good things"]. Another, "pœnam" ["punishment"]. No. 179, "mulcalor". Another, "mulctator" ["one who fines"]. No. 180, "Lucanus" ["Lucan"]. Another, "ut Lucanus" ["as Lucan"]. Ibid., "veniat" ["may come"]. Another, "veniam" ["pardon"]. Ibid., "enervato corpore dedecoret" ["disgraces with an enfeebled body"]. Another, "enervati corporis dedecore" ["with the disgrace of an enfeebled body"]. No. 181, "a mœchia" ["from adultery"]. Another, "a macia". Ibid., "sive a maceratione" ["or from wasting away"]. Another omits [it]. Ibid., "manu ancus" ["crooked in the hand"]. Another, "manu ancus, vel manu cassus" ["crooked in the hand, or deprived of a hand"].
passages.notes: A list of variant readings; the Latin lemmas are kept, with rough glosses in brackets. "A!.", "At." and "AI." are scanning errors for "Al." (alius/alii, another manuscript or edition); "Ibiid." is read as "Ibid." "mulcalor" is probably a misprint or corrupt reading, and is left untranslated. "a macia" is unclear; it is perhaps for "a macie" ("from leanness").

passages.original: 102, partes. Al., partes sunt. Ibid., gignendæ sobolis. Al., a gignenda sobole. Ibid., quod his. Al., quod in his. IV. 108, et crurnm. AI., et crurium. N. 109, dicant. Al. om. Ihid., Ennius. Al., Ennius ait. Ibid., voluit. Al., cogit. Ibid., venirent. Al., perveniret. N. 110 qui iis. AI., quia in his. N. 111 ,rotundi. Al., rotundum. N. 113, stabile. Al., subtilius. N. 1 16, sub corio, est. Al. om.
passages.english: 102, "partes" ["parts"]. Another [reading]: "partes sunt" ["are parts"]. In the same place, "gignendæ sobolis" ["of begetting offspring"]. Another: "a gignenda sobole" ["from the begetting of offspring"]. In the same place, "quod his" ["that to these"]. Another: "quod in his" ["that in these"]. No. 108, "et crurum" ["and of the legs"]. Another: "et crurium" [variant form, "and of the legs"]. No. 109, "dicant" ["they say"]. Another omits [it]. In the same place, "Ennius". Another: "Ennius ait" ["Ennius says"]. In the same place, "voluit" ["he wished"]. Another: "cogit" ["he compels"]. In the same place, "venirent" ["they came"]. Another: "perveniret" ["it reached"]. No. 110, "qui iis" ["who to these"]. Another: "quia in his" ["because in these"]. No. 111, "rotundi" ["round", plural]. Another: "rotundum" ["round", singular]. No. 113, "stabile" ["stable"]. Another: "subtilius" ["more finely"]. No. 116, "sub corio, est" ["under the hide, is"]. Another omits [it].
passages.notes: A list of manuscript variants ("Al." = alii/aliter, another reading; "Ibid." = at the same number; "N." = number) to Isidore, Etymologies book 11 (on the human body); the Latin lemmas are kept with literal glosses since the variants themselves are the content. Scanning errors corrected: "IV." read as "N." (number), "AI." as "Al.", "Ihid." as "Ibid.", "crurnm" as "crurum", "1 16" as "116". The passage opens with the end of an entry begun in the preceding context ("Num. 102").

passages.original: CAP. XVIII. Num. 2, Varro. At. , ut Varro. N. 3, scribit. A!., scripsit. Ibid., humilitatem. A!., humiditatem. Ibid., abruptum. Al., obruptum ; al., obrutum. Ibid., quibus hinc. A!., cujus hinc. N. 4, monstrosam. A!., mons ruosam. N. 5, ubi laniata.
passages.english: CHAPTER XVIII. No. 2, Varro. Another [reading]: ut Varro. No. 3, scribit. Another: scripsit. Ibid., humilitatem. Another: humiditatem. Ibid., abruptum. Another: obruptum; another: obrutum. Ibid., quibus hinc. Another: cujus hinc. No. 4, monstrosam. Another: monstruosam. No. 5, ubi laniata.
passages.notes: Variant readings; the Latin forms are kept. 'At.' and 'A!.' are read as 'Al.'. 'mons ruosam' is read as 'monstruosam'. The variant for 'ubi laniata' follows in the next passage.

passages.original: CAP. XIX. N. 1, cui mirum. At., cum mirum. Ibid., illud inest ut dum. Al. om. lbid., reddat. At., reddit. N. 2, excidat. Al., excindat. Vulcanius conjicit exedat, quia Plinius ait exest, et perrumpit vasa. Ibid., patina. At., patena. Ibid., tum. Al. cum. Ibid., distilat. Al., stillat; Grialius, destillat, sed alibi distillat, quod perinde est. N. 3, scrupulum. A!., scripulum.
passages.english: Chapter 19. No. 1, "to which [it is] wonderful." Others, "since [it is] wonderful." Same place, "this is in it, that while." Others omit. Same place, "it may render." Others, "it renders." No. 2, "it may fall out." Others, "it may cut through." Vulcanius conjectures "it may eat away," because Pliny says "it eats away and bursts through vessels." Same place, "dish" (patina). Others, "patena." Same place, "then" (tum). Others, "when" (cum). Same place, "distilat." Others, "stillat" [drips]; Grial, "destillat," but elsewhere "distillat," which comes to the same thing. No. 3, "scruple" (scrupulum). Others, "scripulum."

passages.original: Ibid., replicata. Al., res implicata. Ibid., pinna. Al., penna. Ibid., avena. Al. add. : « Avena per v liueram herba est, per b verum lorum, quo equi retinemur. Avena herba se- miualis segeti simitis. Virgilius : Urit enim hui campum seges, urit aveæ. Ponitur et pro calamo aliquoties. » Ibid., lolium... A I., lolium herba amarissimi seminis. N. 106, flamma est. Al. add.: I Fenum, quod est palea, per e solam scribendum ;
passages.english: Same place, "folded back" (replicata). Others, "a thing entangled." Same place, "pinna." Others, "penna" [feather]. Same place, "oat" (avena). Others add: "Avena with the letter v is a plant; with b, a strap (habena), by which horses are held back. Avena is a plant of seed, like a crop of grain. Virgil: 'For a crop of flax burns the field, oats burn it.' It is also sometimes used for a reed-pipe." Same place, "darnel..." Others, "darnel, a plant of very bitter seed." No. 106, "is flame." Others add: "Fenum, which is chaff [hay], is to be written with e alone;
passages.notes: "liueram" = litteram, "se- miualis" = seminalis, "simitis" = similis, "retinemur" = retinentur, "hui" = lini, "aveæ" = avenae; "verum lorum" probably corrupt for "habena, lorum". The added note breaks off and continues in the following passage.

passages.original: CAP. x. Num. i, emittantur. A!., add. : « Harum usus primum in insulis quæ Baleares dicuntur inventus eat. Virgilius : Balearis verbera fundæ. » N. 2, colligatis. Al., collectis.
passages.english: Chapter 10. No. 1, "are sent out." Others add: "Their use was first discovered in the islands which are called the Balearics. Virgil: 'the lashes of the Balearic sling.'" No. 2, "bound together." Others, "gathered."

passages.original: Al., Græco nomine. N. 8, navim. At. navem. Ibid., gnavum. A!., gnarum. N. 10, durconem. At., duconem; al., dulconem. Ibid., dicitur. At. om. Ibid., transibit. AI., transivit. iN. 12 , Horatius. Al., Horatius ait. N. 13. dictæ ab eo. At.. vocatæ ab eo. Ibid., collidamur. Al., elidantur. N. 14 , dromo. AI., dromon; al., droma. Ibid., decurrendo dicitur. Al., decurrendo dictus. Ibid., vocant. Luc., vocant, sive a drometis.
passages.english: Others, "by a Greek name." No. 8, "navim" [ship]. Others, "navem." Same place, "gnavum" [diligent]. Others, "gnarum" [knowing]. No. 10, "durconem." Others, "duconem"; others, "dulconem." Same place, "is called." Others omit. Same place, "will cross." Others, "crossed." No. 12, "Horace." Others, "Horace says." No. 13, "named from it." Others, "called from it." Same place, "may be dashed together." Others, "may be dashed out." No. 14, "dromo." Others, "dromon"; others, "droma." Same place, "is called from running." Others, "named from running." Same place, "they call." Lucas, "they call, or from the dromets."
passages.notes: "durconem" etc.: ship-name variants, not identified. "Luc." probably an editor or manuscript; "drometis" uncertain.

passages.original: CAP. XII. Num. i, ut Lucilius. Al., ut Lucius. Ibid., laquearium. A!., laquearium famt.
passages.english: CHAP. XII. No. 1, "as Lucilius [says]". Other [manuscripts read]: "as Lucius". In the same place, "of the panelled ceilings". Other [manuscripts read]: "of the panelled ceilings, [...]".
passages.notes: This is a list of variant readings keyed to Isidore's text. "Al." (alii, i.e. other manuscripts or editions) is printed once as "A!.", a scanning error. "Num. i" is probably "Num. 1". The final word "famt" is unclear and probably corrupt. It may stand for a form of "fames" or another variant word, and it is left untranslated as [...].

passages.original: Ibid., vestes ad corpus contrabat. A I.. vestiat corpus, contrahat. A!., vestium corpus contrahat. Ibid., dicunt. A!., vocant. N. 6, alligat. At., alliget. N. 7, vin( itur. Al., vinciatur. N. 8, Virgilius. AI., Virgilius dicit.
passages.english: Same place, "draws the garments to the body." Others, "may clothe the body, may draw together." Others, "may draw together the body of the garments." Same place, "they say." Others, "they call." No. 6, "binds." Others, "may bind." No. 7, "is bound." Others, "may be bound." No. 8, "Virgil." Others, "Virgil says."

passages.original: Al., afficitur. N. 10 . polluimus. AI., solvimus. N. 12, proxima. Al., proximo. Ibid., antecœnia. Al., antecæna. Ibid., vocantur. Al., vocabatur. A!., vocabantur. N. 13, sic Martialis. AI., sicut Martialis. Ibid., quod et usque. Al., quod ad usque. N. 14, cœna vocatur. A!., cænam vocari. Ibid., vespernam. Al., vespertinam. Num. 15, cum cibo. Al., cum omni cibo. Ibid., fermentatius. Al., fermentarius.
passages.english: Others, "is affected." No. 10, "we pollute." Others, "we loosen." No. 12, "nearest" (proxima). Others, "proximo." Same place, "antecoenia" [appetisers]. Others, "antecaena." Same place, "are called." Others, "was called." Others, "were called." No. 13, "so Martial." Others, "as Martial." Same place, "which also up to." Others, "which right up to." No. 14, "is called dinner." Others, "[that] dinner is called." Same place, "vesperna." Others, "evening [meal]." No. 15, "with food." Others, "with all food." Same place, "more leavened." Others, "leavening."

passages.original: 21, violenti. Al., violento. N. 23, quando ardet in oleo. At., cum ardeat in oleo. N. 24, lardum eo quod. Al., lardus dicitur eo quod. Ibid., repositum. Al. repositus. Ibid., unde Afranius. Al., unde dicit Afranius. Ibid., in Rosa. Al., in prosa. Ibid., sagatum. Al., saginatum. N. 27, mista. Al., commista. Ibid., pulpa autem... glutinosa sit. Al. om. N. 28, lucanieæ. Al., lucaniæ. N. 29, quod fiat. At., quod fit.
passages.english: 21, violenti. Another [reading]: violento. No. 23, quando ardet in oleo. Another: cum ardeat in oleo. No. 24, lardum eo quod. Another: lardus dicitur eo quod. Ibid., repositum. Another: repositus. Ibid., unde Afranius. Another: unde dicit Afranius. Ibid., in Rosa. Another: in prosa. Ibid., sagatum. Another: saginatum. No. 27, mista. Another: commista. Ibid., pulpa autem... glutinosa sit. Another omits [it]. No. 28, lucanieæ. Another: lucaniæ. No. 29, quod fiat. Another: quod fit.
passages.notes: Variant readings; the Latin forms are kept. 'At.' is read as 'Al.'. 'lucanieæ' may itself be a misprint for 'lucanicæ' (sausages).

passages.original: CAP. v!. Num. 3, et sicula. Al., et situla. Ibid., nos siculam. Al, nos situlum; a!.. nos siculam. Ibid., cantharus... Goth. i Tol. add. : Cantharus vas qua... Virgilius : Et gravis appendebat canlharos ansa. N. 4, per diminutionem. Al., per derivationem. Ibid., vocant. A I., dicunt. N. 6, cilicises. A I., cilices; al., cilicienses N. 7, volunt. At. om. Ibid., in quod.
passages.english: Chapter 6. No. 3, "and sicula." Others, "and situla" [bucket]. Same place, "we [call it] sicula." Others, "we situlus"; others, "we sicula." Same place, "cantharus..." The Gothic Toledo [manuscript] adds: "Cantharus, a vessel which... Virgil: 'And a heavy cantharus hung by its handle.'" No. 4, "by diminution." Others, "by derivation." Same place, "they call." Others, "they say." No. 6, "cilicises." Others, "cilices"; others, "cilicienses." No. 7, "they wish." Others omit. Same place, "into which."
passages.notes: "Goth. i Tol." taken as "Gothic Toledo manuscript"; the added text is defective ("vas qua...").
